races.title: State Senate, District 28
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Joe Lisuzzo
cands.bio: Los Angeles businessman who owned Al Gelato, a restaurant and ice cream company on Robertson Boulevard, for about 32 years. Elected member of the South Robertson Neighborhood Council. Republican candidate for State Senate District 28 in 2026, 2022, and in a 2021 special election for District 30.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California, Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association and Reform California are among the endorsements Ballotpedia lists for his 2026 campaign. The list also includes several voter-guide recommendations.

cands.gaps: We could not find where he grew up or when he moved to California. We found no record of his positions on data centers, development or growth, foreign or institutional ownership of homes and land, guns, abortion, school choice or teacher pay. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022 or 2026, and the campaign page's questionnaire was cut off partway through, so his remaining answers could not be read. He has held no legislative office, so there is no legislative record to report. The only office found is the neighborhood council seat, which comes from his own campaign materials. The campaign site also carries unrelated interior-design text, which we ignored.

local.label: Roots 55: Ballotpedia says he was born in Chicago, and the record shows him running a Los Angeles business for about 32 years and earning degrees from CSUN (1999) and UCLA (2001), but it does not say when he arrived in California or where he grew up.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Owned and operated Al Gelato, a Los Angeles restaurant and ice cream manufacturing business, for about 32 years, hiring hundreds of people and running payroll. Elected member of the South Robertson Neighborhood Council. No legislative or policy-staff experience found.
qual.why: Business owner and manager of long standing puts him in the middle band. A neighborhood council seat is a civic board and adds nothing, and no legislative, law, policy or budget career was found.
qual.label: Business owner and manager of long standing puts him in the middle band. A neighborhood council seat is a civic board and adds nothing, and no legislative, law, policy or budget career was found.

back-police-order.evidence: Said in a Southern California News Group questionnaire that law enforcement 'must always be funded and never defunded' and that he is a strong proponent of law and order.

workers-first.evidence: Said in the same questionnaire that state government should work 'hand in hand with the federal government when it comes to "illegal anything"' on immigration, and that he would end Medi-Cal coverage for undocumented immigrants.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: Said in the same questionnaire that he would fight to save and maintain Proposition 13 for current and future California homeowners. He also said he would eliminate the state gas tax and cut waste, fraud and abuse in government. He did not say he would end homestead property taxes.

prio.label: Matches 3 of 3 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 3 only promised

cands.name: Lola Smallwood-Cuevas
cands.bio: Democratic member of the California State Senate for District 28 since December 2022. Former journalist, SEIU Local 1877 organizer and UCLA Labor Center project director. Co-founded the Los Angeles Black Worker Center. Chairs the Senate Labor, Public Employment and Retirement Committee.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, Working Families Party, California Federation of Labor Unions, California Nurses Association, California Teachers Association, National Union of Healthcare Workers, California Environmental Voters and Equality California.
The Los Angeles Times endorsed her 2022 State Senate bid.

cands.gaps: We could not find where she was born, where she grew up, or when her family moved to California. We found no statements or actions from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, H-1B or immigration enforcement, gun policy, or school choice. We found nothing on development or growth limits beyond her support for infill housing streamlining, and no documented controversies. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022 or 2026. The issues page on her campaign site was cut off before the Environment section, so anything further there was not read.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: State Senator since December 2022, serving on the Budget and Fiscal Review Committee, after a career as a journalist, SEIU Local 1877 organizer and UCLA Labor Center project director (2004–2022, about 15 years as project director). Co-founded the LA Black Worker Center.
qual.why: Nearly four years of legislative service plus a long labor-policy and research career place her in the high band for writing law and the budget. Her committee chairmanship was not counted.
qual.label: Nearly four years of legislative service plus a long labor-policy and research career place her in the high band for writing law and the budget. Her committee chairmanship was not counted.

pro-life.evidence: Calls herself a champion of keeping California a safe haven for people seeking reproductive healthcare and abortion services.

back-police-order.evidence: Wrote on her campaign site that the number of police on the street alone does not make neighborhoods safer, and that the justice system should center on diversion, rehabilitation and de-escalation rather than a surveillance and incarceration approach.
